title: Study Round Record
description: The body a round writes at its integrate step. Replaces the study's arms wholesale rather than patching them: a whole-file rewrite cannot leave the state half-updated, and a partial write on an interrupted round is the one corruption this design refuses to be exposed to.

arms.description: Every arm the study knows about, in rank order. Written whole each round.

arm.description: Stable identifier, reused across rounds so a reader can follow one arm's history.

kind.description: What kind of problem this is, which decides the ceiling formula and where the work can go. Named rather than inferred, because a candidate routed by its symptom instead of its cause reaches somewhere that cannot act on it.

status.description: `in_flight` means a job exists and nothing else may assume its result.

claim.description: One line: what this arm asserts would help.

share.description: Amdahl bottleneck share in [0, 1]: measured fraction of total step/request time attributed to this bottleneck in the baseline profile (e.g. 0.40 if a kernel takes 40% of step time).

headroom.description: Addressable fraction in [0, 1] of `share` this arm claims it can eliminate (e.g. 0.50 for a 2x kernel speedup; `share * headroom` = 0.20 expected end-to-end ceiling gain).

blocked_on.description: Required in spirit for a blocked arm: what is needed and who can give it.

claimed_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when an executor or worker claimed this arm for in-flight execution (defaults to America/Los_Angeles PDT/PST; configurable via TPU_AGENT_SUITE_TIMEZONE).

claimed_by.description: Identifier of the worker or process holding the active in-flight claim.

summary.description: One-line conclusion or summary recorded when an arm is released or evaluated.

failed_dispatches.description: How many dispatches of this arm ended `failed` with no verdict: an implementation the executor could not repair, not a tested idea. Counted by `study release-arm --failed`, which blocks the arm when it reaches the cap, so an arm nobody can implement does not take every remaining round.

release_reason.description: Deprecated alias for `summary` when an in-flight arm was released.

result.description: Present once the arm is decided. Carries the measurement, not a summary of it.

verdict.description: `tie` is the default and the burden is on `win`. `invalid` means the measurement cannot be trusted or violates admissibility constraints (cannot count), which is different from a result that did not help (`loss`, performance regression below the noise floor).

execution_id.description: The single execution that produced this measurement -- a compute job id, not a session or run id. This is what makes a gate's same_execution requirement checkable instead of decorative.

replicates.description: How many times it was actually measured, which is not necessarily what the protocol asked for.

delta_pct.description: Change against the study's baseline. Compared to the protocol's noise floor to separate a win from a tie.

provenance.description: A closed set. Not `verified`, not `confirmed`, not `derived`. A modelled ceiling reported where it reads as measured is the most common way a study starts believing its own predictions.

gates.description: One entry per gate the protocol declares. A gate the protocol requires and the result omits is a missing check, not a passing one.

execution_id.description: Which execution this gate was measured on. When the protocol marks the gate same_execution, this must equal the metric's execution_id: throughput from one run and accuracy from another do not describe the same configuration.

artifacts.description: Paths to durable outputs. Referenced, never inlined, so a round stays cheap to read.

next.description: The one thing that unblocks the next round, and when it can happen.

arms.claim: fuse the dequant epilogue into the MoE GEMM
